metaDescription: USM CH 2 cacao is a cacao variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: USM CH 2 is a registered cacao variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2014 as NSIC 2014 Cc 13. Its record notes about 2.35 tonnes of dry beans per hectare a year.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. Its record notes about 2.35 tonnes of dry beans per hectare a year. It first bore pods about 20 months after planting. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

blocks.text: It was weak against coffee/pod borer, so scout for it from the early weeks.

The pests and diseases that hit cacao fields most often: [black pod of cacao](/diseases/cacao-black-pod), [cacao pod borer](/pests/cacao-pod-borer), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant USM CH 2 cacao

Plant grafted clones, and mix two or three, because many cacao clones need another clone nearby to set pods. Pick by pod yield and bean size. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of USM CH 2?
